chapter.title: Plugging in your work apps

cards.body: Your line from chapter 1 wakes up on time, but right now it can't touch a single one of your work apps. Every station that reaches into Gmail, Google Sheets or Slack needs a key card: a **credential**, a saved permission that lets n8n work inside one app for you. You make the card once and hang it on a hook, and any station on any line can borrow it.
cards.simpler: Your line from chapter 1 now wakes up on time. But it still can't touch any of your work apps. Any station that reaches into Gmail, Google Sheets or Slack needs a key card. That key card is a **credential**: a saved permission that lets n8n work inside one app for you. You make it once and hang it on a hook. Then any station on any line can borrow it.

cards.prompt: You drag a Slack station onto your line so it can post 'New lead!' in #sales-wins. What does it need before it can do anything?

options.text: A second trigger, so Slack knows when to listen
A saved permission from Slack to post there
A copy of the Slack app installed inside n8n

whyNot.a: That's the bell, not the key card: the line already has a trigger, and a trigger only decides when the run starts.
whyNot.c: That's installing the app, not getting permission: n8n already knows how to talk to Slack and only needs your OK.

cards.reteach: The station already knows how to talk to Slack. What it doesn't have is permission. A credential is that permission, saved once, so the station can walk into Slack with a badge Slack itself handed over.

cards.title: What the key card is
cards.body:
A *credential* is a small saved record that says: this n8n may act in this app, for this account. With most work apps, n8n never even sees your password.

You make one from inside a station. Open a Slack or Google Sheets node, find the *Credential to connect with* box and create a new one. Slack or Google opens its own window, lists what n8n wants to do, and you click Allow.

n8n stores it encrypted (scrambled, so nobody can read it off the disk). Here's the useful part: **one card works on every line you build**.
cards.simpler: A credential is a small saved note: this n8n may act in this app, for this account. Most work apps never show n8n your password. To make one, open a Slack or Google Sheets station and create a new one under *Credential to connect with*. Slack or Google opens a window listing what n8n wants to do. You click Allow. n8n stores it scrambled so nobody can read it. And **one card works on every line you build**.

cards.title: Priya's first row
cards.body: Priya runs office ops and keeps a sheet called 'Visitor Log – Oct'. She adds a Google Sheets node, picks *Append Row*, creates a credential and clicks Allow in the Google window that pops up. Suddenly the Document dropdown lists her own sheets: **that list is the proof the key card works**. She presses the button to run just that step (Test step or Execute step, depending on her n8n version), and a row reading 'test test' appears. Three weeks later it's still there, because nobody will ever delete it.
cards.simpler: Priya runs office operations and keeps a sheet called 'Visitor Log – Oct'. She adds a Google Sheets station, picks *Append Row*, creates a credential and clicks Allow in the Google window that pops up. Right away, the Document list shows her own sheets. **That list is the proof the key card works.** She presses the button that runs just that step (called Test step or Execute step, depending on the version), and a row saying 'test test' appears. Three weeks later it's still there, because nobody will ever delete it.

cards.prompt: On Monday, Sam made a Slack credential for his 'Standup reminder' line. On Wednesday he builds a second line that also posts to Slack. What should he do in the new Slack station?

options.text: Pick his Monday Slack credential from the dropdown
Make a fresh Slack credential, one per line
Type his Slack password into the message text

whyNot.b: That's a new key card when he could reuse the old one: one card per app per account is enough, and duplicates get confusing fast.
whyNot.c: That's a password, not a credential: anything in the message text gets posted for everyone to read.

cards.reteach: A credential belongs to an account and an app, not to one workflow. Picture one key card on a hook by the door: every station on every line borrows that same card. Make it once, then pick it from the list.

cards.title: It only opens the doors it's given
cards.body:
You'd think plugging n8n into Slack gives it some special robot access to the whole company. It doesn't. **A credential only opens the doors it was given.** A Google credential borrows your account, so the station reaches exactly what you can reach and nothing more.

If you can't open the finance team's budget sheet in your own browser, your Sheets station can't open it either. Slack is often set up as a bot instead, and a bot can usually only post in channels it's been invited to.

Either way, whatever the station does, it does in front of real colleagues. Test in a channel or sheet only you can see first.

Either way, it acts in front of real colleagues. Test first in a channel or sheet only you can see.

cards.body: Leo connects Google Sheets on a Friday afternoon while his browser is signed into his personal Gmail. The Document dropdown fills with 'Wedding budget' and 'Sourdough log' instead of 'Q4 Leads', and he spends 20 minutes sure that n8n is broken. The sign to look for: **if the file list looks like the wrong part of your life, check which account the credential belongs to**. Put the email in each credential's name, like 'Sheets – leo@work', so you can tell at a glance.

cards.prompt: Your Sheets station fails because it can't find 'Team Budget 2026', a sheet your manager owns and never shared with you. The trigger fired fine. What's the most likely cause?

options.text: The trigger needs to fire at a different time
The credential acts as you, and your account can't open that sheet
Every sheet needs its own separate credential

whyNot.a: That's the bell, not the key card: the run already reached this station, so the trigger did its job.
whyNot.c: That's one card per sheet when it's really one per account: a single Google credential opens every sheet your account can open.

cards.reteach: A Google credential is your badge, not a master key. The station walks into Google as you, so it can't open any sheet you can't open in your own browser. Once your manager shares the sheet, the same credential will work.

cards.title: In one breath
cards.body:
Picture the hooks by the door. One Slack card that both of Sam's lines borrow. One Google card that fills Priya's visitor log every morning, and still can't open 'Team Budget 2026', because nobody shared it with her.

That's a credential: a saved permission for one app, made once, reused by every line, opening only the doors it was given.
cards.simpler: Picture the hooks by the door. One Slack card that both of Sam's lines borrow. One Google card that fills Priya's visitor log, but still can't open 'Team Budget 2026', because nobody shared it with her. That's a credential: a saved permission for one app. You make it once, every line reuses it, and **it opens only the doors it was given**.

cards.body:
Open n8n, add a Google Sheets or Slack node and create one credential with your work account. Rename it to include your email. If you run n8n on your own computer, n8n's docs cover the extra Google setup.

Tomorrow: the lead's name your form caught at station 1 shows up, spelled right, in station 3's Slack message.
cards.simpler: Open n8n, add a Google Sheets or Slack station, and make one credential with your work account. Then **rename it so the name includes your email**. If you run n8n on your own computer, Google needs some extra setup, and n8n's help pages walk you through it. Tomorrow: the lead's name your form caught at station 1 shows up, spelled right, in station 3's Slack message.

chapter.outcomeLine: You can now connect one work app to n8n and make it add a row or send a message.

dubious_claims: The Slack 'acts as you' framing (badge, can't post in #leadership): n8n's Slack credential is often a bot token or OAuth app that posts as the app, not as you. The bot has to be invited to a channel, and your own channel memberships don't directly limit it.
The 'Test step' button: newer n8n versions call it 'Execute step', so a reader may not find the label as written.
repairedFrom.why: The 'In one breath' teach card is pure abstraction with no thing, place or moment, so it fails concrete_images. Its 'Tomorrow' teaser is the chapter's only open loop, but the try card follows it, so the chapter ends on a note about n8n's docs instead.
repairedFrom.fix: Rewrite card 9 around one image, e.g. 'one key card on the hook, borrowed by Sam's standup line and Priya's visitor log, and it still can't open your manager's Team Budget 2026.' Then move the teaser to the last line of the try card and make it sharper: 'Tomorrow: the lead's name your form caught at station 1 shows up, spelled right, in station 3's Slack message.'
